title: Fake Merc Character Study (part. 18): Looking lean, Bison
summary: Part 18 of NH's mocking series on YouTuber Jason Blaha. He credits Blaha's public apology to veterans, analyses his 620 lb charity deadlift as showing no progress (deadlift bar, deadlift-only, no weight class), revisits fake-plate suspicions, relays a former teen client's account of Blaha's coaching (low-volume training, huge calorie jumps, 'all weight is muscle'), and ridicules his diet. Along the way he makes points on bulking rate, deadlift bars and food quality.
claims: NH delayed the series a month because Blaha publicly apologized to veterans after a charity deadlift event, as NH had demanded
A deadlift bar (longer, thinner, whippier) adds roughly 20-30 lb to a 600 lb pull versus a stiff bar, per elite deadlifter Cailer Woolam
A deadlift-only event without prior squat and bench, and without a weight class, inflates a deadlift compared with a full powerlifting meet
Blaha's 620 lb deadlift-bar pull equals roughly his old 585 lb stiff-bar competition pull, so in four to five years he has made zero progress or regressed
To disprove fake plates, a lifter should show the plates, load them and pull without cutting the camera
Blaha's clients mostly find him through old fitness pages shilling his 5x5, not through his channel; most leave after two to three months
Blaha claims a 27 FFMI, above Arnold's roughly 25-26; NH estimates his own FFMI at around 23-24
Very low-volume training built around one-rep-max squats and deadlifts is not enough volume for a teenager to grow
Bumping a teen's calories from 3,500 to 4,300 (+22%) to gain 1 kg a month is miscalculated and will produce far more than 1 kg, mostly fat; 800 kcal is an extra meal
Gaining weight is not the same as gaining muscle; getting heavier and moving more weight is not true strength gain
Food is anabolic only in the sense of building mass; it drives muscle gain only if you train, otherwise you just get fat
Telling a client who is getting fat to keep eating to 'build a base', and raising calories 60% to force 3 kg a month, fosters eating disorders and obesity in kids
Undereating is not killing your gains; force-feeding teenagers facilitates eating disorders
Ketosis requires cutting carbs; a gallon of milk a day contains enough carbs to break keto
In the vertical diet, orange juice is meant to boost appetite, never to replace vegetables
Boiling red meat ruins its nutrients and taste
Gaining 10 lb in a week without noticing is implausible on a clean diet; it implies eating a lot of junk on top
Early tooth decay is linked to later heart problems
A body-fat scan proves nothing without a baseline scan to compare against
GOMAD-style force-feeding may suit very athletic people burning thousands of calories, not sedentary lifters
